components.name: Map packages
components.desc: Downloads, updates, switches off and deletes the optional map packages (base map, landscape, ancient world, gazetteer, roads) in ☰ → Instruments → Map.
components.detail: The list of packages comes from `maps/maps.json`; the files themselves come from the lesepult-maps site and are kept whole in the Cache 'pult-maps', where the service worker serves them as ordinary `maps/…` addresses. Installed versions and switched-off packages are remembered in the settings (`mapPk`, `mapOff`). Only 'Base map' is required; packages with two levels of detail are one row with a choice, and installing one level removes the other.

mem: a downloaded file is joined in memory before it is stored (up to ~40 MB for the largest)
store: Cache 'pult-maps': ~21 MB base map, +25 MB landscape, +7–39 MB roads, ~4 MB each for gazetteer and ancient layers

components.netNote: downloading needs the network; installed packages work offline

components.name: Package list and status
components.desc: Knows which map packages exist, which are installed and which are switched off.
components.detail: `mapManifest` fetches `maps/maps.json` (6 s time-out) and keeps a copy in 'pult-maps', falling back to that copy offline. `mapInstalled` reads the setting `mapPk` (and migrates the old 'ancient' package into its two halves); `mapOff` reads `mapOff`; `mapHas` combines both. `mapsEnabled` always answers yes now (the map can no longer be switched off as a whole). `MAPS` also names the cache 'pult-maps' (MAPCACHE).

store: maps.json copy in 'pult-maps', two small settings

components.netNote: fresh list online; the cached list offline

components.name: Download and delete
components.desc: Fetches a package file by file, resumes broken downloads, and removes packages again.
components.detail: `downloadMapPkg` fetches every file from the package's own address (lesepult-maps), up to three tries each; big files come as numbered parts that are parked in Cache 'pult-dl-parts' (tagged with the version) so a stopped download continues where it broke off, then joined into one Blob and stored in 'pult-maps'. Afterwards the other level of the same group is deleted, the gazetteer index is rebuilt for 'places', and the map is rebuilt if its style changes. `downloadMapQueued` is the entry used by the download queue of dialogs.js (progress on the row's button). `deleteMapPkg` keeps files that another installed package still uses.

mem: parts of one file held as Blobs and joined (up to ~40 MB, est.)

components.netNote: needs the network to download; deleting works offline

components.name: Instruments → Map section
components.desc: The rows of map packages in the Instruments dialog, with level choices, switches and 'Rebuild place index'.
components.detail: `mapSectionHTML` groups the manifest into Basic / Appearance / Gazetteers (`MAP_GROUPS`), folds regional packages, hides retired packages unless still installed, and appends the saved relief areas of maprelief.js. `redrawMapSection` re-renders it in place keeping the scroll position; `mapSummary` gives the 'n packages installed' line. When a package is switched on or off, `mapPkChanged` throws the map away and rebuilds it (and the places of the text for 'places'); `applyMapsOn` shows or hides the map tab button.

components.name: Gazetteer (place index)
components.desc: The ancient places of the Pleiades gazetteer (~34,500 places), indexed on the device so names in texts can be looked up fast.
components.detail: The index is built once from `places/places.json` of the 'places' package and kept in its own IndexedDB 'pult-places'. Reading a text loads only the name bundles and places it needs; opening the map loads every place. Each place gets a significance rank 0–9 that decides which dots and names show when zoomed out.

mem: all places as objects while the map is open (est. 20–40 MB)
cpu: building the index once takes seconds

components.name: Place database
components.desc: The IndexedDB 'pult-places' where the place index lives, read in bundles.
components.detail: `plDB` opens 'pult-places' with four stores: p (places, in bundles of 512 = `PB`), k (name keys, hashed by `plHash` into 1,024 bundles), id (place id → number, 512 bundles) and meta (info, ranks). Bundling makes writing a few hundred large records much faster than 100,000 small ones. `plGet`/`plGetMany` read records; `plKey` keeps up to ~1,100 recently read name bundles in memory; `placeIndexInfo` reads the build info; `dropPlaceIndex` clears everything (when the package is deleted).

mem: cached name bundles (est. a few MB)

components.name: Building the index
components.desc: Turns the downloaded gazetteer file into the on-device index.
components.detail: `buildPlaceIndex` fetches `maps/places/places.json` (3.7 MB, served from 'pult-maps' by the service worker), turns 34,463 rows into place objects, corrects start dates from titles ('Late Roman province' → AD 284), and collects exact-name keys and stem keys for the Greek, Latin and romanised names; stem keys only for main kinds of places (`MAIN_TYPES`), and generic first words like 'Ager' or 'Mons' are skipped (`GENERIC`). It ranks the places, then writes all bundles in transactions of 4,000. It runs after the package is installed or updated, on 'Rebuild place index', or when first needed.

mem: whole JSON parsed plus two key maps (est. 40–80 MB briefly)
cpu: once, several seconds on a phone (est.)

components.name: Name keys
components.desc: Normalises Greek and Latin names so that different spellings and endings meet.
components.detail: `translit` turns Greek letters into the Latin spelling used by the gazetteer (rough breathing → h, γγ → ng, diphthongs). `exKey` is the exact key (the app's `gkey`). `stemKey` merges spelling variants (ae/e, k/c, ph/f, y/i, double letters) and strips common case endings, keeping at least three letters.

components.name: Loading places
components.desc: Brings places from the database into memory: only those needed while reading, all of them for the map.
components.detail: `loadPlaceIndex(full)` rebuilds the index if the package version changed, then either loads every place bundle (`getAll`) for the map or starts an empty table for reading; it also loads your own places (`pown|` settings). `placesLoad` and `placesLoadIds` fetch single bundles on demand and drop the rest of each bundle. `placeById` also finds your own places ('o…' ids); `hasType`, `isRegion`, `isPeople`, `isWater` and `typeLabel` classify a place by its gazetteer types.

mem: all ~34,500 place objects with the map open (est. 20–40 MB)
cpu: loading all bundles when the map opens

components.name: Significance of places
components.desc: Gives every place a rank 0–9 so that zoomed out only the important places get dots and names.
components.detail: `placeScore` weighs links from other places, population, mentions in the library and on this device, number of names, city status, having both Greek and Latin names, and a penalty for rough positions (`SIG_DEF`, adjustable with sliders `SIG_UI` in the map settings). `rankPlaces` sorts by score and hands out ranks by position (top 30 → 9, next 50 → 8 … `RANK_TOP`), then saves the ranks to 'pult-places' after 1.5 s. `storeCounts`/`loadDevCounts` keep per-text counts (`pcnt|`), and `countDevice` reads every text on the device to count them; `recomputeSig` re-ranks and refreshes the dots.

mem: a score array for all places
store: ranks in 'pult-places', a count per text in settings
cpu: sorting 34,500 places on each weight change; 'Count the places in all texts' reads every text (minutes, est.)

components.name: Searching the gazetteer
components.desc: Finds places by name while correcting a place on the map.
components.detail: `searchPlaces` loads the whole gazetteer if needed, then scans all places for names starting with the typed text (exact key) or with the same stem, stopping after 31 hits. It runs 200 ms after typing stops.

cpu: a linear scan of ~34,500 places per search

components.name: Places in texts
components.desc: Finds the place names in any text by looking up the lemmas of proper nouns in the gazetteer, picks the most likely place, and lets the reader correct it.
components.detail: Works for every text, also imported ones, entirely on the device. Ambiguous or doubtful matches are flagged ('to check'). Corrections are stored per passage, per work or everywhere. 'Places from' decides which texts and which part of them feed the map.

mem: hits per text and caches for other parts of the work
cpu: scanning a text and scoring candidates, after each text is opened

components.name: Finding names
components.desc: Picks out the words of a text that may name a place and their candidate places.
components.detail: `findPlaceHits` goes through the tokens, keeps capitalised words, and skips words analysed as ordinary words, adjectives, verbs, Roman numerals and sentence-initial function words (`FUNC_WORDS`). It reads all name bundles the text may need at once, then `placeCands` looks up the exact key (and, for unanalysed words, the stem key, main places only), at most 40 candidates. Neighbouring words give hints: 'flumen', 'urbs', 'ποταμός' say what kind of place (`CUES`); 'filia', 'uxor' or titles like 'Caesar', 'rex' next to it say it is a person (`PERSON_CUES`, `TITLE_CUES`). `plainName` strips vowel-length marks from Latin names.

mem: name bundles of the text (let go afterwards)
cpu: per text, after the lemmas are known

components.name: Choosing the place
components.desc: Decides which of several same-named places a word means, and how sure that is.
components.detail: `choosePlaces` applies the reader's corrections first (`pl|`, `plw|`, `plg|` settings), drops places first attested clearly after the work's date (`workYear`: the reader's date or the author's from the catalogue), then scores candidates by closeness to the unambiguous places nearby in the text and to the text's 'home region', by fame (names, city, rank) and by the cue word. A result is marked uncertain as 'later', 'person', 'ambiguous' or 'form' (stem only). `dictSaysPerson` reads the beginning of the dictionary entries for the name and counts whether most call it a person or a place. `textKeyOf`/`workKeyOf` give the keys under which corrections are stored.

cpu: per text; dictionary look-ups per name

components.name: Places of the open text
components.desc: Marks the place names in the open text and offers a map button in the dictionary entry of a place word.
components.detail: `placesForText` runs after the lemmas of the open text are resolved (called from analysis.js): it loads the reading part of the index, finds and chooses places, stores counts, refreshes the map if open. `markPlaces` adds the classes `plc` (and `plcq` for uncertain) to the words in the text pane. `mapIconForView` puts a small Europe button next to the headword in the dictionary view when the word is a place.

store: a count per text in settings

components.name: Places of other texts
components.desc: Finds the places of other books of the work, or of any text in the library, without opening them.
components.detail: `placesOfPart` reads another book of the open work from the library database, tokenises it, applies the treebank annotation or the morphological analysis for lemmas, and runs the same finding and choosing; results are cached per work (`M.workCache`). `placesOfAny` does the same for any text id (book or imported text), caching in `M.anyCache` and storing counts.

mem: tokens and hits of every text read for a multi-text map (est. several MB per long work)
cpu: analysing whole works; can take seconds per book

components.name: Correcting places
components.desc: Lets the reader confirm, change or remove the place of a word, for one passage, the work, or everywhere.
components.detail: The card's 'change' panel (`changeHTML`) lists other places of the same name with their distance, a gazetteer search, 'Pick on the map …' (a new own place) and 'Back to the automatic choice'. `saveCorrection` stores the choice under `pl|text|word`, `plw|work|name` or `plg|name`, re-runs the recognition, and offers to apply the same to the other passages of that name. `checkPop` lists all uncertain places of the part ('⚑ n to check') with one-tap confirm or reject; `UNSURE` holds the reasons shown.

components.name: Places from: range
components.desc: Works out which places the map shows: of this section, chapter, book, work, the author's works or the selection.
components.detail: `scopeRange` turns the current reference into a word range (in verse, blocks of 20 or 100 lines via `isVerse`/`verseBlock`; chapters by `chapterKey`). `scopePlaces` collects the places in that range (or across all books of the work, or via `multiPlaces` across several texts), counting passages and names and leaving out unconfirmed 'later' places. `scopeParts`, `refRange` and `eachScopeHit` list the texts and word ranges of the author or selection and walk their hits. `scopeLabel` gives the button text ('chapter 3', 'lines 1–20').

cpu: on every refresh; more for author/selection (reads many texts)

components.name: Places from: menu and selection
components.desc: The 'Places from' menu at the top of the map and the editor of a saved selection of works, books, chapters and sections.
components.detail: `scopePop` shows the on/off switch, the six steps (`SCOPES`) and a sentence explaining what is covered (`scopeExplain`). `selPop` edits the selection ('+ this section/chapter/book/work', remove); `selItem`/`selAdd` build an item from what is being read; `selBrowse` opens the library as a tree (chapters are read when a book is unfolded, verse in 100-line blocks). `selKey`, `selSummary` and `shortWork` name and compare items. The selection is saved in `mapCfg.sel`.

cpu: browsing reads books to list their chapters

components.name: Map start-up and engine
components.desc: Opens the map pane: loads the map engine from the downloaded base package, builds the map and wires its controls; shows a clear message when something fails.
components.detail: The engine is MapLibre GL (version 5, or 4.7 for old downloads) read from 'pult-maps'; PMTiles packages are read straight out of the cache. Start-up runs in named steps with a 25 s watchdog so that a hang shows the step it stopped at. Map settings live in one object (`M.cfg`) saved as the setting `mapCfg`.

mem: MapLibre with its tile caches and GeoJSON sources (est. 100–250 MB on a large screen)
cpu: style building and tile parsing in workers
gpu: one WebGL canvas redrawn while moving

components.name: Map scripts check
components.desc: Makes sure the map's script files have run before the map starts.
components.detail: `ensureMapScripts` checks that maplayers.js, mapsaved.js, mapdraw.js and maprelief.js defined their main functions; a missing one is loaded once more from the website with a cache-busting query. Script errors of map files are collected in `SCRIPT_ERR` (by a global error listener) and shown if the map cannot start.
components.netNote: reloading a missing script needs the network

components.name: Loading MapLibre
components.desc: Loads the map engine from the base map package.
components.detail: `engineDir` picks `base/lib5/` (MapLibre 5) when it is in the cache, else `base/lib/` (4.7). `loadMapLib` adds the stylesheet and the script (version 5 is first patched by `shadePatchedLib` of maprelief.js), then pmtiles.js if present. `inCache` checks 'pult-maps'; `addScript` is a promise wrapper also used by maprelief.js; `mapLibP` makes it happen once.

store: engine files are part of the base package

components.name: Reading PMTiles from the cache
components.desc: Lets the map engine read tiles out of single-file packages kept in the cache.
components.detail: `pmInit` registers the `pmtiles://` protocol with MapLibre. `pmUrl` returns that address for a downloaded package file (landscape, Blue Marble, Itiner-e roads, relief) and registers a `CacheSource`, whose `getBytes` slices the requested byte range out of the cached Blob (`pmBlob`, one Blob per file kept for the session).

mem: Blob handles per package file; tile bytes sliced on demand

components.name: Opening the map
components.desc: Builds the map pane and the MapLibre map, step by step, or says why it could not.
components.detail: `showMap` runs `showMap1` once at a time with a 25 s watchdog. `showMap1` checks the base package, collects the files of installed and switched-on packages, loads the ancient labels, the full gazetteer and the drawings, writes the pane's HTML (buttons, time bar, card, pop-up), loads the engine, imagery catalogues and relief, then creates the `maplibregl.Map` (globe, pitch up to 85°, zoom 0–16) at the last position (`mpos|last`). It hooks map events: labels on every move (one per frame), fewer dots when zoomed out, saving the position, taps (picking a point, drawing, places, drawings, roads, rivers), WebGL context loss. `mapFailed` shows the error with 'Try again', 'Reset the map settings' (old settings kept as `mapCfgOld`) and 'Use the previous map engine'.

mem: the MapLibre map and its sources (est. 100–250 MB)
cpu: building the style and first tiles

components.name: Map state and settings
components.desc: The shared map state and the map settings with their defaults and migrations.
components.detail: `M` is the one global object of the map (the place index, the MapLibre map, the selected place, hits, caches). `mapCfg` loads the setting `mapCfg` once, upgrades older settings (scope names, layer menu v5, retired base maps, sun and moon size) and merges it over the layer defaults `LCFG`; `saveMapCfg` writes it back. Also used by dialogs.js for backup and restore.

components.name: Globe, flat map and 3D
components.desc: Switches between globe and flat (Mercator) projection and turns 3D terrain on or off.
components.detail: `viewOn` reads `cfg.globe`/`cfg.t3d` (both on by default). `viewToggle` sets the projection or the terrain (`T3D`: source 'terrdem' with the reader's exaggeration, default 1.5) without moving the camera, and updates the obelisk shadow. `mapPt` projects a point to the screen and, on the zoomed-out globe, moves points on the far side off screen so their labels are not drawn.

gpu: 3D terrain adds mesh work per frame

components.name: Map tab and controls
components.desc: The map button in the toolbar, and the dispatcher for all buttons inside the map pane.
components.detail: The toolbar button shows a small Mediterranean image (`EUROPE_ICON`); tapping toggles the map (`toggleMapTab`), holding opens Settings → Map. `wireMapUI` wires one click handler on the map pane that routes to the card, corrections, the check list, 'Places from', layers, saved maps, drawing, relief and globe menus, and one input handler for the gazetteer search. The page-level code of maps.js also blocks page zoom gestures over the map, handles package switches and 'Rebuild place index' in Instruments, the dictionary's map button and the display switches of the map settings.

components.name: Places on the map
components.desc: Shows the places as dots and names, lets the reader tap one and opens its card with the passages that name it.
components.detail: The base style holds land, lakes, rivers and borders from the base package and the place dots; names are HTML labels laid over the map so Greek and Latin appear in the reading font, without overlaps, most important first.

cpu: labels redrawn once per frame while moving

components.name: Base map and place dots
components.desc: The base layers (sea, land, lakes, rivers, modern borders) and the dots of the places shown.
components.detail: `mapStyle0` builds the MapLibre style from the GeoJSON files of the base package (land 0.9 MB, lakes 0.6 MB, rivers 1.8 MB, borders 0.2 MB) plus an empty 'places' source and the dot layers 'pl'/'pl-region', then hands it to `layerStyle` for all other layers. `mapStyle` adds the glyph address for contour numbers, the projection and the globe's halo. `mapColors` gives light or dark colours. `refreshMapData` writes the current places into the 'places' source (size by number of passages, faded when uncertain), updates the 'Places from' button and the check count, then re-applies the layers.

mem: base GeoJSON parsed in workers (est. 20–40 MB)
cpu: on each refresh; tiling the GeoJSON in workers

components.name: Place names
components.desc: Draws the names of the places on top of the map, without overlaps.
components.detail: `drawLabels` takes up to 220 places in view, most important first (the selected one always), measures each name on a hidden 2D canvas in 'Gentium Book Plus', skips any that would overlap, and writes HTML spans; the boxes are kept for tapping (`M.lblHit`). Then it adds the names of your own places and drawings and the region/site names of the layers. `labelOf` names a place as the text does, in English, or by its modern name (setting); `cleanT` strips '(river)' and '?' from gazetteer titles.

cpu: once per animation frame while the map moves

components.name: Tapping places
components.desc: Finds the place meant by a tap, or offers a short list when several are close.
components.detail: `tapPlace` queries the rendered dots within a fingertip (22 px on touch, 10 px with a mouse), weighs distance against significance when zoomed out, prefers a tap right on a name, and opens `chooserAt` – a small list of up to 8 places at the finger, most significant first – when it is not clear.

components.name: Place card
components.desc: Selects a place and shows its card: name, kind, height, and the passages that name it, each leading back into the text.
components.detail: `selectPlace` (from the text, the map or a list) remembers the map position per word, eases the map to the place and calls `showCard`, which lists the passages in this part with a few words of context, '⚑' reasons, 'change' and 'Not a place here', and adds the ground height from the relief. `mapForWord` and `mapWordTapped` connect the text: a tapped word shows its place, or offers 'Mark as a place …'. `cardWork` searches all books of the work, `cardMulti` all texts of the author or selection. `mapGo`/`mapGoAny` open the passage (on a phone the text replaces the map). `closeCard` clears the selection.

cpu: searching a whole work or selection reads many texts

components.name: Scale bar, zoom and units
components.desc: A reference distance and the zoom level in the corner, and the units used for all distances and heights.
components.detail: `mapInfo` computes metres per pixel at the map centre and shows a bar of a round length (≤110 px) in the chosen unit; it runs once per frame with the labels. `UNITS` defines metric, imperial, Roman (mile 1,479 m, foot 29.6 cm) and Greek (stade 185 m, foot 30.8 cm); `unit` gives the chosen one and `fmtEle` formats heights (also used by the relief).

components.name: Layers
components.desc: Everything the map can show on top of the base map – all gazetteer places by kind, the ancient world, roads, names of regions – and the Layers menu that switches them.
components.detail: `layerStyle` assembles one MapLibre style from the base map and the layers of every module (imagery, rivers, drawings, relief, sun), and `layerProps`/`applyLayers` set visibility, filters and opacity from the settings and the period filter.

mem: GeoJSON sources of the ancient world (~4 MB files) and 34,500 site points
cpu: re-applying filters on every period change

components.name: Style assembly
components.desc: Puts all layers into one map style and keeps their visibility, filters and opacity in step with the settings.
components.detail: `layerStyle` adds: the detailed landscape (PMTiles; exact coasts, lakes and rivers from zoom 5, inside 20°W–80°E, 0–62°N), the ancient-world layers (coastline of the period, areas of regions and peoples, empires with colours `EMP_COL`, provinces, roads, canals, aqueducts, walls, city outlines), Itiner-e roads (certain solid, conjectured dashed, hypothetical dotted), your own places, drawings, the all-places dots, then imagery, OSM rivers, relief and sun. `layerProps` computes for each layer id its visibility, filter and paint from `M.cfg` and the period filter (Barrington roads hide when Itiner-e is installed); `applyLayersTo` applies them before the style is built, `applyLayers` on the live map (and redraws labels).

mem: parsed GeoJSON sources (ancient roads 2 MB, empires 0.6 MB …)
cpu: rebuilding the style; applyLayers on every change

components.name: All places by kind
components.desc: With 'Places from' switched off, shows every place of the gazetteer as a coloured dot by kind (settlements, sanctuaries, forts …).
components.detail: `sitesData` turns every place (except purely modern ones) into a GeoJSON point with its category (`SITE_CATS`, 11 kinds with light and dark colours), rank and dates, cached as `M.sitesFC`. `siteCats` gives the kinds ticked in the menu (settlements by default); `dotMinW` hides less significant dots when zoomed out (rank ≥7 below zoom 3.5 … all from 6.5); `siteFont` sizes names by rank.

mem: a 34,500-point GeoJSON source and its tiles (est. 10–20 MB)
cpu: tiling the points in a worker on each setData

components.name: Names of regions, peoples and sites
components.desc: Writes the names of regions, peoples, mountains, islands and seas along their lines, and the names of all places when every place is shown.
components.detail: `loadAncientLabels` reads `ancient/labels.json` (0.5 MB) once and keeps, for each label, its longest line, end points and bounding box. `moreLabels` (called by `drawLabels`) places up to 160 of those in view, longest first, rotated along their line with letter spacing, faded by the period filter and coloured by period if chosen; then, with 'Places from' off, up to 180 site names from the rendered dots, biggest rank first, smaller and fainter when zoomed out.

cpu: once per frame while moving (text measuring, rendered-feature query)

components.name: Roman road card
components.desc: A tap on a road of Itiner-e shows what is known of it.
components.detail: `roadTap` queries the three Itiner-e road layers within a fingertip and fills the card with the road's name, main or secondary, certainty of the course, dates, the itineraries naming it and its builder (Itiner-e, CC BY 4.0).

components.name: Layers menu
components.desc: The menu of the layers button: Places, Political, Built world, Names on the map, Your own – folded groups with counts of what is on.
components.detail: `layersHTML` builds the groups with toggles (`tgl`), segmented choices (`segc`) and fold sections (`foldSec`, fold state remembered), showing 'Needs the download …' where a package is missing. `rightPop` shows such a menu at the right side of the map and remembers its scroll position (also used by the relief and globe menus); `layersPop` opens it, `refreshLayersPop` re-renders it after a change. `layerClick`/`layerClick1` handle every button of the menu, the period buttons and the map settings: changing a value saves `mapCfg` and either re-applies the layers or rebuilds the style (units, base map, imagery).

cpu: on taps; a style rebuild for some settings

components.name: Map settings
components.desc: The map settings (hold the map button, or ☰ → Settings → Map): display, units, places in texts, period options, significance weights.
components.detail: `settingsHTML` builds the section: scale bar, zoom level, size of sun and moon, the look of rivers, the ArcGIS key, units, jumping to places, persons, names, tolerance, how faded/hidden things show, period colours, slider range and default view, significance sliders and 'Count the places in all texts'. `mapSettingsDialog` shows it as a dialog; dialogs.js also embeds it. The page-level code of maplayers.js handles its inputs (default view, slider range, period colours, weights) and closes map menus on a tap outside.

components.name: Period filter
components.desc: A time slider at the foot of the map: one date, a period or up to five periods; the map shows what existed then and fades or hides the rest.
components.detail: Applies to empires and provinces (at the date), areas, roads, aqueducts, walls, all places and your own drawings, with a tolerance in years. It starts at the date of the work.

cpu: while dragging, filters of many layers are re-applied once per frame

components.name: Dates and periods
components.desc: Keeps the dates chosen on the slider and formats years.
components.detail: `M.T` holds the ranges for the open work (`timeFor` starts with the work's date). `snapY` rounds to the slider's step; `tRanges` adds the tolerance; `snapRanges` gives the ranges without it (for things of one date, like empires); `normRanges` merges touching ranges; at most five (`TMAXR`). `fmtY`/`fmtR` write '380 BC', 'AD 117', '480–323 BC' (also used by the library).

components.name: Filters and fading
components.desc: Turns the chosen periods into map filters, opacities and colours for the layers and labels.
components.detail: `tOpacity` builds a MapLibre expression from each feature's y0/y1: inside a period full, gone before it faded or hidden (`tGoneO`), known only from later sources faded by default (`tLateO`), undated per setting (`tUnd`); `tIn`, `tGone`, `UND`, `Y0`/`Y1` are its parts. `tFilter` hides what is fully transparent; `snapFilter` selects what belongs to the date. `tState` is the same in JavaScript for HTML labels. `tColor` gives each period its colour when 'Each its colour' is chosen (`RANGE_COL`, `rangeCol`).

cpu: MapLibre re-evaluates the expressions per feature

components.name: Time slider
components.desc: The bar with its scale: tap for a date, hold to make a period or split one, drag ends to change, pinch or wheel to zoom the scale.
components.detail: `timeBarHTML`, `axisHTML` (as many round-year marks as fit) and `renderTime` draw the bar, the ranges, their handles and a mark at the work's date. `wireTime` handles pointers on the whole bar: one finger moves ends, periods or the scale; long press (550 ms) turns a date into a ~90 px period or splits a period; ends snap together and join; two fingers or the wheel zoom (`setView`, at least 20 years, saved after 400 ms). `timeChanged` re-renders and re-applies the layers once per frame. `TLIM`, `tDefView`, `tView`, `tStep`, `tPct` give the limits (4000 BC–AD 2050), default view (1000 BC–AD 800) and step (1, 5 or 10 years).

cpu: per pointer move: re-render and a layer update per frame

components.name: Date of the work
components.desc: Lets the reader set the date of a work, used for its places and as the slider's start.
components.detail: `workDateDialog` asks for a year ('380 BC', 'AD 117'), stores it as `wyear|<work>` (or resets to the author's date), then re-runs the recognition of places and resets the slider.

components.name: Imagery and online waters
components.desc: Photographic base maps (NASA Blue Marble offline; Sentinel-2 and Esri online) and, online, the rivers and lakes of OpenStreetMap.
components.detail: Blue Marble from the base package always lies beneath any online imagery, so gaps show Blue Marble instead of nothing; going offline or online rebuilds the style.

mem: raster tile textures in MapLibre's cache (est. 20–60 MB)
store: Blue Marble 15.8 MB in the base package; catalogues in settings

components.netNote: Blue Marble offline from the package; Sentinel-2, Esri, NASA tiles to zoom 8 and OSM rivers online

components.name: Imagery sources
components.desc: Decides which imagery is shown and where its tiles come from.
components.detail: `imgKind` is the reader's choice (Blue Marble, Sentinel-2 or Esri). `imgOnline` returns the online raster source: NASA GIBS Blue Marble to zoom 8 (`GIBS_BM`), EOX Sentinel-2 cloudless by year via WMS (`EOX_WMS`, to zoom 15), or Esri World Imagery – current with a free ArcGIS key (`ESRI_CUR`) or an earlier Wayback capture (to zoom 19). `bmPkg` gives the Blue Marble PMTiles of the base package (`BM_PKG`); `imgOn` says whether any imagery can be shown; `isOnline` reads `navigator.onLine` (also used by relief and sun).
components.netNote: online sources need the network; the package works offline

components.name: Imagery versions
components.desc: Keeps the list of Sentinel-2 years and Esri Wayback dates the reader can choose from.
components.detail: `imgInit` loads the ArcGIS key and the saved catalogue (`imgCat`) and, online, refreshes it at most once a week in the background: `imgCatalogs` reads EOX's WMS capabilities (`EOX_CAPS`) for the s2cloudless years and Esri's Wayback configuration (`WAYBACK_CFG`) for the capture dates. `s2Versions` falls back to a built-in list (`S2_DEF`, 2016, 2018–2024); `waybackVersions` gives the dates (used by the globe menu).
components.netNote: refreshed online once a week; the saved list offline

components.name: Imagery layers and credits
components.desc: Places the imagery beneath waters, lines and names, and shows the required credits on the map.
components.detail: `imgStyle` inserts the Blue Marble layer and the online layer below the ancient waters/areas or lakes, and adds lake outlines on top (from zoom 5 those of the landscape package). `imgLayerProps` hides the drawn land, sea, lakes and the relief's sea floor and colours while imagery is on. `imgPaint` sets a short fade and linear resampling. `imgCredit` writes the Sentinel-2 / Esri (with Wayback date) and OpenStreetMap credits into the corner.

mem: raster tiles in MapLibre's tile cache
gpu: one or two full-screen raster layers

components.name: Online/offline switching
components.desc: Rebuilds the map's style when the device goes online or offline, or when the imagery choice or the ArcGIS key changes.
components.detail: On the browser's online and offline events `netRelief` re-initialises the relief (Mapterhorn online, packages offline) and then `imgNetChange` rebuilds the style and refreshes places and credits. The page-level code of mapimg.js also handles the imagery select boxes, the ArcGIS key field (kept on this device only) and the river look controls.

cpu: a full style rebuild on each switch

components.name: Rivers and lakes from OpenStreetMap
components.desc: Online, draws rivers, streams, canals and lakes from OpenStreetMap at every zoom; offline the base map's own waters are used.
components.detail: `rivStyle` adds the OpenFreeMap planet vector tiles (`OFM`, OpenMapTiles schema) as 'osm-lakes' and 'osm-rivers' (no tunnels), and gives the offline rivers the same colour and width factor. `rivPaint` colours by kind from strongest (rivers) to weakest (streams) with widths by zoom; `scaleW` scales width stops. `rivLayerProps` hides the offline waters while OSM is shown. `rivSettingsHTML` and `rivRepaint` handle width and colour settings (`RIV_DEF`, `rivCfg`); `osmRiv` says whether OSM is used.
components.netNote: OSM waters online only; Natural Earth/landscape waters offline

components.name: River and lake card
components.desc: A tap on an OpenStreetMap river or lake shows its names and kind.
components.detail: `waterTap` queries the OSM water layers within a fingertip, prefers a named feature, and shows the name with its Latin, English, Greek or local variants, the kind (`RIV_KIND`), whether it dries up at times or crosses on a bridge.
components.netNote: only while the OSM waters are shown (online)

components.name: Drawing on the map
components.desc: Your own places, lines, arrows, areas, freehand lines and texts, in named sets, with lengths and areas, a period, and links to passages; GeoJSON in and out.
components.detail: Every drawing is one setting (`draw|<id>`, own places `pown|<id>`, sets `dset|<id>`) in IndexedDB, so it is saved immediately and included in backups. Drawings are MapLibre GeoJSON layers; their names, texts and lengths are HTML labels like the place names.

store: a few KB per drawing in settings
cpu: small; per frame while dragging points
gpu: a few line and fill layers

components.name: Drawings data
components.desc: Loads, saves and deletes drawings, own places and sets.
components.detail: `loadDrawings` reads all `draw|` and `dset|` settings once (creating the set 'My drawings' if there is none). `dSave`/`dRemove` write or delete a drawing or own place; `dGet`, `dSetOf`, `dKind` look them up; `dNewId`, `dClone`, `r5` (coordinates to 5 decimals) help; `D_KIND` names the kinds.

store: settings draw|, dset|, pown| in IndexedDB 'greekreader'

components.name: Lengths, areas and dates
components.desc: Measures lines and areas on the sphere and writes them in the chosen units.
components.detail: `havKm` (haversine; also used by the relief profile), `lenKm` and `areaKm2` (spherical polygon area as in GIS programs) measure; `fmtKm` gives the length in the chosen unit plus Roman miles and stades, `fmtArea`, `fmtN`, `dLenShort` format; `dMeasure` gives the card text. `dDates` and `parseYear` read and write a drawing's period ('401 BC', 'AD 117').

components.name: Drawing layers and labels
components.desc: Draws the drawings and your own places on the map, with names, texts and lengths.
components.detail: `drawStyle` adds the sources 'draw' and 'drawtmp' and layers for areas, a selection halo, solid and dashed lines, arrowheads and the line being drawn; `drawFC` turns the drawings into GeoJSON (arrowheads computed in screen pixels by `arrowHead`, so they are rebuilt on zoom); `ownFC` does the same for your own places. `dShown` hides switched-off sets and drawings whose passages are not covered; `dState`, `dOpacity`, `dTimeF` apply the period filter; `drawLayerProps` sets visibility and opacity. `drawLabelsOwn` writes names of own places, texts, names and lengths of lines as HTML labels and keeps their boxes for tapping.

cpu: labels per frame while moving; GeoJSON rebuilt on changes

components.name: Drawing mode and tools
components.desc: The pen button's bar: tools (place, line, arrow, area, freehand, text, select), colour, width, dashes, set, undo and Done.
components.detail: `drawToggle` opens the bar (`drawBarHTML`, icons `D_TOOLS` made with the shared `svg` helper, `PEN_ICON`), disables double-click zoom and remembers the tool and style in `mapCfg`. `drawClick` takes taps on the map first: a place or text opens a name dialog (`dAddPoint`, `dAddText`), lines and areas collect points until the last/first point is tapped again (`dFinish` saves, `dTmp` shows the line in progress). `wireFreehand` draws with one finger (the map does not pan; a second finger cancels) and `simplify` (Douglas–Peucker, 1.4 px) thins the stroke. `dUndo` undoes points or whole saves; `dStyleSel` applies colour/width/dash also to the selected drawing; `dInfo` shows the chip with points and length; `drawUIClick` routes all buttons. Page-level code adds Esc, Enter and Ctrl+Z and the set/colour inputs.

cpu: per pointer move while drawing freehand

components.name: Selecting and changing drawings
components.desc: Tap a drawing to see its card; edit its name, note, set, colour, period and passages; drag, add or remove points; delete it.
components.detail: `tapDrawing` finds the drawing under a tap (labels, distance to segments, inside an area). `showDrawCard` shows kind, set, dates, length or area, note, linked passages and – with relief – a height profile. `dEditDialog` edits all properties (also turning a line into an arrow, adding the current section/chapter/book/work as a passage). `dHandles` places drag handles on the points, midpoints (to add a point) and the centre (to move all); `wireHandles` drags them (one update per frame), removes a point on a 550 ms hold, and records undo. `dDelete` asks and removes.

components.name: Drawings linked to passages
components.desc: A drawing linked to passages appears only while 'Places from' covers one of them.
components.detail: `dScopeUpdate` (run with every map refresh) computes which linked drawings to hide: `scopeCoverage` describes what 'Places from' covers now (section range, book, work, author's texts, selection) and `linkCovered` checks each link against it, reading other texts' references when needed (`workOfId`). `dGoLink` opens a linked passage from the card.

cpu: on each refresh, may read other texts

components.name: Sets, import and export
components.desc: Named sets of drawings that can be shown or hidden, renamed, deleted, and exported or imported as GeoJSON.
components.detail: `ownLayersHTML` is the 'Your own' group of the layer menu (switch, sets with counts, new set, import, export all, lengths on/off). `dNewSet` creates a set; `dSetMenu` renames, exports or deletes one with its drawings. `dGeoJSON`/`dExport` write a FeatureCollection with simplestyle colours, lengths and areas (opens in QGIS, geojson.io …). `dImport` reads any GeoJSON (Multi* and collections split up, colours and Pult properties kept) into a new set and fits the map to it.

components.name: Saved maps and export
components.desc: Saves what the map shows to open again later, and exports it as an image, a PDF or a Pult map file.
components.detail: A saved map is one setting `mmap|<id>`: texts, part, view, periods and layer settings. Exports are made on the device and offered as a file to save.

mem: a full-resolution canvas copy while exporting (est. 10–40 MB)
cpu: drawing labels and encoding PNG/JPEG on export

components.name: Saving and opening maps
components.desc: Saves the current map under a name and opens a saved one again.
components.detail: `mapState` records the scope, open text and reference, centre and zoom, the period ranges and the layer settings listed in `MAP_KEYS`. `saveMapDialog` suggests a name and stores it as `mmap|<id>`; `savedMaps` lists them newest first. `openSavedMap` opens the text and passage if needed, restores the settings (rebuilding the style if the base map differs), periods, view, and refreshes.

components.name: Saved maps menu
components.desc: The bookmark button's menu: the saved maps, save, open a map file, export.
components.detail: `savePop` lists the saved maps with delete buttons and the export choices (Image, PDF, Pult map file); `savedClick` handles its buttons and those of the 'Places from' menu and selection editor (switch, edit, add, remove, browse, show).

components.name: Export
components.desc: Exports the map as PNG, PDF or a Pult map file with its places and corrections.
components.detail: `exportMap` names the file from `mapTitle` (work, part and periods). For a Pult map file it bundles the map state, the places shown and all corrections, own places, drawings and sets that belong to the texts (JSON 'pult-map-1'); for PNG/PDF it renders the image. The result is offered through the app's save-file dialog.

components.name: Map image
components.desc: Draws the map as it is on screen, with its labels, a title and the credits, into one picture.
components.detail: `mapCanvas` waits for one map render, copies the WebGL canvas at device resolution, then redraws every HTML label onto it (font, opacity, letter spacing, rotation, a halo in the background colour), adds a 46 px footer with the title and the credits of the layers actually visible (Pleiades, imagery, Natural Earth, OSM, AWMC, Itiner-e, Mapterhorn). Also used by the sun module.

mem: a canvas of screen size × device pixel ratio (est. 10–30 MB)

components.name: PDF writer
components.desc: Wraps the map picture into a one-page A4 landscape PDF.
components.detail: `pdfOf` encodes the canvas as JPEG (quality 0.92) and writes a minimal PDF 1.4 by hand: catalog, page, one image XObject with DCTDecode, a content stream fitting it with 24 pt margins, and the cross-reference table. No PDF library is needed.

components.name: Opening a map file
components.desc: Opens a Pult map file, adding its corrections, own places and drawings, and shows the map.
components.detail: `importMapFile` checks the format 'pult-map-1', asks for confirmation, writes the contained `pl|`, `plw|`, `plg|`, `pown|`, `draw|`, `dset|` settings (replacing yours where they differ), saves the map and opens it. The texts must be in the library.
